case_name: Sukhvinder Pal Bipan Kumar v State of Punjab and Others
facts: The licences held by the petitioners who are food grains dealers in the State of Punjab, have been suspended by orders passed by the District Food and Supplies Controllers, Faridkot and Bhatinda, for a period not exceeding ninety days under the second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order.
The petitioners have all been served with notices under the first proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order to show cause why their licences should not be cancelled.

Some of the petitioners accept that in the recent past their licences were suspended under the second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order for alleged breach of the licence conditions for having sold large quantities of wheat to dealers outside the State without disclosing the names of the purchasers in their stock registers.

The other petitioners allege that because they approached the High Court by way of petitions under Art.226 of the Constitution, complaining against restrictions placed on movement of wheat by rail, their licenses have been suspended under the second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order as a punitive measure.

The State of Punjab in the counter-affidavits filed by the Deputy Secretary to the Government of Punjab, Food and Supplies Department, Chandigarh, and the District Food and Supplies Controller, Faridkot, controvert the allegations of the petitioners.
issues: Whether the second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order confers upon the licensing authority unguided, uncontrolled and arbitrary power to suspend a licence
Whether the suspension of the food grains dealers' licences held by the petitioners was mala fide and motivated
petitioner_arguments: The second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order confers upon the licensing authority unguided, uncontrolled and arbitrary power to suspend a licence
The suspension of the food grains dealers' licences held by the petitioners was mala fide and motivated
respondent_arguments: The second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order does not confer upon the licensing authority unguided, uncontrolled and arbitrary power to suspend a licence
The suspension of the food grains dealers' licences held by the petitioners was not mala fide and motivated
court_reasoning: To make the point intelligible, it is necessary to deal with the scheme of the Order.
Cl.3 of the Order provides that no person shall carry on business as a dealer except under and in accordance with the terms and conditions of a licence granted by the licensing authority.

The power of cancellation or suspension of a licence which was subject to the giving of a reasonable opportunity to the licensee of stating his case was not adequate and sufficient to effectively check and control flagrant breaches of the provisions of the order, during the pendency of the proceedings for cancellation of a licence.

The State Government was evidently of the opinion in the light of the experience gained in the recent past, that for effective control and regulation of the trade in foodgrains, it was necessary and expedient that the licensing authority should be clothed with powers to suspend a licence on the spot when it detects contravention of any of the terms and conditions of the licence or any of the provisions of the Order.

The power of suspension conferred by the second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order is by way of an interim measure, pending the holding of an inquiry as to whether there is any breach which must result in cancellation of the licence.
holding: We are unable to accept any of these contentions.
The power of suspension conferred by the second proviso to sub-cl.(1) of cl.11 of the Order does not satisfy the test of reasonableness.
cases_cited: Sukhvinder Pal Bipan Kumar v State of Punjab
